decisive_items: progressively worsening sharp epigastric pain radiating to the back
No acute abnormality of the pancreas
response.rationale: Acute pancreatitis is supported by classic epigastric pain radiating to back and markedly elevated lipase; CT can be normal early in the course, so the normal pancreas finding does not exclude it. Chronic pancreatitis lacks chronic features and imaging changes, while pancreatic insufficiency lacks acute presentation and specific support.

rejected.why: Decreased oral intake and diabetes are nonspecific; no evidence of malabsorption or chronic pancreatic dysfunction.
Pain pattern alone is insufficient; no prior episodes, chronic imaging changes, or calcifications to support chronic pancreatitis.
